layer1_identification.workType: a thin rectangular slab of focaccia bread with chopped olive pieces pressed into a hand-dimpled top
layer1_identification.broadClassification: food prop / stylized clay-like 3D render, game asset
layer1_identification.note: reference images are themselves AI-rendered stylized clay renders, not photographs; target look is soft matte clay, not photoreal

layer2_form_silhouette.boundingVolume: thin rectangular slab (extruded rounded rectangle), flat top and bottom
layer2_form_silhouette.symmetry: rectangular footprint, broken by organic corner rounding and a slightly wavy/torn perimeter edge (visible vertical creases on the side wall in the front-elevation view)
layer2_form_silhouette.shapeLanguage: geometric base form with organic surface treatment (hand-dimpled, hand-torn edge)

derivedRatios.topDownAspect: width:depth roughly 3:2 (rectangular, longer than deep, matches base focaccia.ts HALF_X=1.0/HALF_Z=0.65)
derivedRatios.cornerRounding: corners visibly rounded, not sharp right angles

meso: side wall (plain crust, faint vertical tear striations)
micro: finger-pressed dimples: each individually oval, uneven rim, varied depth -- not a stamped circle
olive chunks: irregular hand-chopped polygonal wedges, each with its own tilt/size, most seated in or beside a dimple, half-sunken
oil pools: small round-ish glossy amber pools inside a minority of the dimples only
rosemary needles: a few sparse thin green slivers resting on the surface, not embedded
salt flakes: a small sparse scatter of tiny bright white specks

layer4_spatial: <olive chunk, embedded-in, dimple> contact: embed, half-sunken -- dough visibly hugs the chunk's edges (not resting on top)
<olive chunk, beside, dimple> contact: some chunks sit adjacent to a dimple rather than centered in one, overlap/rest
<oil pool, embedded-in, dimple> contact: embed, fills the concave dimple interior, no chunk present in that dimple
<rosemary needle, resting-on, top face> contact: flush-with, thin sliver laid on the surface, not pressed in
<salt fleck, resting-on, top face> contact: flush-with, tiny surface speck
no floating parts; every topping sits on or in the slab's top face

crust.relief: soft rounded bumps and dimples, smooth clay shading (not faceted in this v4 render)

oliveChunk.roughness: slightly lower than crust -- a small soft specular highlight is visible on the top of several chunks, distinguishing it from the fully matte dough
oliveChunk.relief: irregular fractured polygonal chunk, not a smooth dome; a visible darker pit-hole/fracture mark near the chunk's center on several pieces

oilPool.roughness: low -- glossy, a small bright specular highlight is visible, the only clearly glossy surface in the whole object
oilPool.translucency: semi-translucent amber pool, flat and following the dimple's concave floor

layer5_materials.runtimeNote: consumer runtime force-replaces every material with MeshLambertMaterial keeping only map+color (types.ts section 2), so the olive/oil gloss distinction above is not reproducible at runtime -- color contrast is the only channel available and is treated as the dominant cue instead

layer6_color.source: assets/prompts/breads/focaccia--olive-flesh.json v4 geometry.crust (authoritative, hand-transcribed, JSON overrides image on any conflict)
layer6_color.finish: crust matte; olive near-matte with a faint highlight; oil pool glossy
layer6_color.observedVsSpec: rendered olive reads slightly warmer/lighter than raw #3B2F2F in the lit crop (small top highlight), and the top-down crop reads the crust a touch cooler/lighter than the 3/4 crop -- CRIB 'fix the measurement plane' lesson: top-down is the reference plane, and per CRIB the lighting rig was just recalibrated so no gain/parity correction is applied here, hex used as-is

layer7_identity_features: hand-dimpled top: each dimple visibly different -- oval not circular, rim uneven, depth varies -- this is the single most identity-defining trait distinguishing it from the base focaccia.ts's regular 5x4 grid
olive chunks are irregular hand-chopped wedges (not uniform 'kiss' domes), roughly 9-11 visible pieces, clustered loosely with quiet plain gaps between clusters rather than spread evenly
oil pools appear in only a minority of dimples (2-4 out of the total dimple count visible across views), the rest of the dimples stay plain (empty finger marks)
sparse rosemary + salt accents, not a dense scatter
side wall shows faint vertical tear/crease texture in the front-elevation view (organic hand-stretched dough edge, not a perfectly smooth extruded wall)
layer8_uncertainty: underside is fully occluded in all three views; modelled as a plain flat crust cap, never visible above the horizon
exact dimple/chunk coordinates are not identity-critical beyond count, irregularity, and loose-cluster-with-gaps distribution -- procedurally seeded

top-down view shows a slightly different apparent olive count/spacing than the 3/4 view due to perspective foreshortening in the 3/4 shot; top-down is treated as the count/spacing reference per CRIB's 'fix the measurement plane' rule
the v4 render is smooth-shaded (no facets), consistent with the pipeline's 2026-08-30 smooth-finish decision -- no conflict to resolve there
side-wall tear striations are a nice-to-have, not scored as a mustMatch feature given the 2-material budget is already spent on crust/oil/olive
